chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Walad, who said: I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

about a sick man who acknowledged at the time of death to an inheritor that there was a debt for him upon himself. He (peace be upon him) said: That is permissible. I said: So if he were to bequeath to the inheritor something? He (peace be upon him) said: Permissible.
ai.seo_question: Is a debt acknowledgment by a dying person to an inheritor valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the debt acknowledgment of a dying person in favor of an inheritor, resolving the potential conflict between debt repayment and inheritance distribution. This ruling ensures that creditors who are also heirs receive their due without reducing the shares of other heirs, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing settled debts over residual inheritance. The permissibility of specific bequests to heirs further clarifies that such gifts do not require the consent of other heirs, provided they do not exceed the one-third limit typically associated with wills.
